inherited_methods.method: totally additive function for repetitions-allowed products
inherited_methods.loss_step: replace Finset occurrence differences in {-1,0,1} by arbitrary integer multiplicities
inherited_methods.lost_information: the same integer cannot be used twice on one side in the active variant
inherited_methods.consequence: the linear-functional characterization applies to the excluded repeated-factor problem but not here; {2,4} is an exact mismatch witness

inherited_methods.loss_step: compress the whole exponent vector to one additive count and require that count to equal one
inherited_methods.lost_information: distinctness could permit nonlinear circuit control outside a single additive hyperplane
inherited_methods.consequence: the entire mechanism has density at most 1/e by lambda exp(-lambda)<=1/e

inherited_methods.loss_step: verify only relations whose larger side has at most L factors
inherited_methods.lost_information: minimal unbalanced circuits can have arbitrarily many distinct squarefree factors
inherited_methods.consequence: K_(s+1,s) edge-prime products give a minimal (s+1)-versus-s relation inside every fixed high-tail cutoff once s is large

inherited_methods.loss_step: multiply every occurrence in a repeated relation by the same free parameter
inherited_methods.lost_information: an unbalanced relation has different homogeneous degrees on its two sides
inherited_methods.consequence: the common parameter appears to powers r and s and destroys equality; nonlinear repair lies on a sparse set not forced by natural density

inherited_methods.loss_step: use an arbitrary rational or integer kernel vector as though it were a {-1,0,1} circuit
inherited_methods.consequence: linear rank deficiency alone does not produce a forbidden Finset relation

inherited_methods.loss_step: assign a different certifying prime to every admitted integer
inherited_methods.lost_information: only pi(N)=o(N) prime labels are available up to N
inherited_methods.consequence: private labels cannot certify a density-one subset; reused prime fibres need a new peeling theorem

inherited_methods.loss_step: stop after enumerating the finite minimal-relation hypergraph
inherited_methods.lost_information: uniform structure as N grows and relations between separately optimized blocks
inherited_methods.consequence: finite optima are exact kill tests only and do not imply either density statement

inherited_methods.loss_step: treat local admissibility in disjoint numerical intervals as hereditary across their union
inherited_methods.lost_information: multiplicative relations can use factors from several blocks
inherited_methods.consequence: finite part ii does not automatically yield a natural-density set for part i

required_new_information: A deletion or admission theorem controlling every minimal {-1,0,1} unbalanced exponent circuit, including arbitrarily long squarefree K_(s+1,s) circuits, with total deletion o(N).
Or an ordered largest-prime-fibre peeling rule that exposes an endpoint of every minimal unbalanced circuit and proves bounded total congestion.
For any auxiliary-element amplification, an all-scale supply theorem showing that a density-one candidate must contain the nonlinear auxiliary pattern.
For SAT/ILP, a symbolic completeness theorem reducing all large-N obstructions to a bounded family; raw optimum values do not count.
A separate natural-density gluing theorem if the finite construction is pursued first.
